To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immunosuppressant abatacept reduced Tregs in the synovial membrane of patients with PsA.

abatacept treatment is associated with significant clinical improvement, reduced synovitis and vascularity on arthroscopy and MRI, reduced expression of FOXP+3 regulatory T cells in the synovial tissue and reduced expression of CD4, CD8, CD3 and CD45RO in the skin of patients with PsA.
abatacept reduces Treg expression in synovium but does not affect Treg expression in lesional skin of PsA patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that the T cell plays in the development of autoimmune diseases such as multiple sclerosis and psoriasis.
the role of regulatory T cells in psoriatic arthritis and the effects of abatacept treatment on synovial and cutaneous inflammation.
the study of a novel treatment for psoriatic arthritis and the mechanisms of its action in this disease.

this was a small, single-centre study, which was not blinded and did not include a control group, and that the results need to be confirmed in a larger study.
this study demonstrated that the expression of FOXP-3+ cells, especially CD4+FOXY-3+ cells in synovial tissue, was decreased in patients with Psoriatic Arthritis after Abatacept treatment.
this study demonstrates that abatacept is an effective treatment option in patients with active PsA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
abatacept is an efficacious treatment option for joint inflammation in psoriatic arthritis.
the study demonstrated that abatacept is an effective treatment for joint disease in PsA.
we demonstrated that abatacept is effective in reducing synovial Tregs and improving joint-related clinical outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
abatacept is effective at reducing the expression of Treg cells in synovium of patients with PsA but not in the skin.
abatacept reduces synoviocyte T-cell expression, which may explain the clinical efficacy in PsA patients with synovitis.
we have shown for the first time that the immunosuppressive function of Tregs in the synovial tissue of patients with PsA is reduced following 5 months of abatacept treatment.
